newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU scientists say no BSE risk from cows milk - report.
newsitem.headline: EU scientists say no BSE risk from cows milk - report.

text.p: EU scientists said in a report on Tuesday that there is no risk of tranmission of the disease bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) from cows' milk.
"There is no evidence that bovine milk transmits BSE. They (committee members) are therefore of the opinion that bovine milk can be safely consumed in any form by any species," the report said.
The EU's scientific and veterinary committee nonetheless said that current controls that prohibit the consumption of milk from clinically suspect cattle should be maintained.

The report, issued by the European Commission, also concluded that current controls should be extended to include colostrum from cattle suspected to have BSE but added that exceptions can be made for both colustrum and milk from such cattle used to feed a cow's own calf.
The European Union imposed a worldwide ban in March 1996 on all exports of British beef and derived products in order to protect public health.
The ban followed a British government admission of a probable link between BSE and a deadly human equivalent, Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD).
